speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For my Ministry, we see the extent of the problems because we deal with the individuals and their families who suffer from it.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This is the reality that we grapple with.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We do not under-estimate the impact that problem gambling has on individuals as well as families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We are not in favour of gambling; we do not encourage it; and we do not want to promote it amongst our people.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We share fairly similar perspectives that many Members have with regard to this issue.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: However, taking that position does not preclude the fact that gambling will exist.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is something that others who engage in it have different viewpoints on.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Like it or not, it is something that people participate in, in some form or other.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Our basic concern really is this: as far as remote gambling is concerned, it is an area that is growing.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We look at what is happening around the world; it is proliferating; it is growing significantly.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In Singapore, where the Internet penetration rate is particularly significant and smart devices abound, there is a very high probability that this is something that would become more of an issue with time.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We share very significant concerns with regard to that, which is why two years ago, we debated in this House the Remote Gambling Act.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In that Act, there were the provisions for the exempt operator regime, because we believe that even though we may take a very robust position with regard to managing this space, we are all familiar with the Internet – it is impossible to completely regulate it.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: There will be ways to bypass – by VPN, proxy sites and so on – for those who wish to engage in online gambling.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: While we take a very robust position, having a tightly managed, controlled space with safeguards put in place would allow those who continue to gamble online to have a space where at least some level of management can take place.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: That is the approach that we are taking with this issue at hand today.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: MSF works very closely with MHA to develop a range of social safeguards for the exempt operators (EOs) to implement, to protect young persons and other vulnerable persons from the harms of remote gambling.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The EOs have to carry out stringent checks to verify the identity of the applicant, such as a face-to-face verification at physical outlets with a valid NRIC/FIN and screening of existing casino exclusions with the National Council on Problem Gambling (NCPG), before an account can be opened.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Page: 10 To protect financially vulnerable individuals, persons who have been excluded from casinos due to family objection or their financial situation will not be allowed to open an individual account.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Individuals can also apply to exclude themselves from remote gambling.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Funding limit means the maximum amount that can be transferred or deposited into the account per calendar day, while expenditure limit means the maximum amount that can be used for betting per calendar day.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Once they have reached their expenditure limits, they will no longer be allowed to place any bets for the rest of the day.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: As an additional safeguard, any request to increase their expenditure limit will only take place the next day, while requests to reduce their expenditure limit will be effective immediately.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: NCPG has been active in rolling out prevention programmes to complement the stringent safeguards for remote gambling.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For example, NCPG partners TOUCH Cyber Wellness and Fei Yue Community Services to deliver cyber wellness roadshows and talks to students and parents.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: NCPG also launches public education campaigns and videos to highlight the risks of problem gambling.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: One of the recent videos has a backdrop of sports betting and illegal online betting, to educate youths on spotting the signs of problem gambling and helping their friends in need.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Another features popular getai emcee Wang Lei relating his struggles with problem gambling and the importance of family support in helping him recover from problem gambling.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: While the Government puts in place stringent safeguards, complemented with NCPG's public education efforts, personal responsibility as well as family and community support are still essential to address this complex issue of problem gambling.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Essentially, what we are doing is to put in place a robust set of laws to have a tightly managed space with safeguards, having an extensive effort as much as possible to raise awareness and have public education and provide support measures for those with these issues.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We all understand the ills that come with this.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We all would like to take a strong position with regard to this and we do take that, although we also recognise the reality is that, given the Internet space, we would not be able to completely remove the possibility of people gambling online.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We believe that having a tightly managed space with safeguards put in place would help at least to ameliorate some of those concerns, even as we continue to work hard on the other measures in place.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: First, if, after the EOs start their trade, the number of Singaporeans moving into online gambling increases, will the Government review its decision regarding the two exemptions?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do carry out surveys to have a sense of the number of people who are gambling and how many of them are gambling online.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will track the 	Page: 11 numbers and see how those compare over time, but we do not have definitive numbers of who exactly are online today.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are not able to fully track that.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will track in terms of survey, in terms of responses and see how those numbers grow and we will assess the situation accordingly.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Similarly, with gambling addiction, we find through surveys, the overall numbers have largely remained quite stable.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do see more coming forward to seek treatment.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That, we believe, is also due to greater awareness and public education.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Again, in terms of data, as we begin to track some of these things more definitely, we are able to then detect trends and patterns to see how we can deal with it accordingly.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: If we need to tighten measures and review policies, we will continue to do so.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: In my view, there is actually a basis for comparison.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: My question is: how many were gambling online illegally during that 20-month total ban period?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: My suggestion is to compare that figure with the numbers after the exemptions.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: That is a possible test, in my humble view.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: My questions are: if the online gambling cases go up, would the Minister consider removing the exemptions and implement a complete ban?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are not able to track all of them.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Those that we are able to track, we have taken some operations.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: MHA will be able to elaborate on some of the details and actions against those who have violated the laws.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: What we have are indicators in terms of the overall market and how it is growing globally.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is not just a problem that is faced by a local market.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: What we have are participation rates from surveys, from when we survey Singaporeans on how many of them are engaged in some form of gambling and, for those who are gambling, how many of them would engage in some form of online gambling.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Obviously, when they do that, they would be in an illegal space.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But in terms of his specific position, that we have been able to know the specific numbers in the course of the last one year plus, we would not be able to do that.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Those who are gambling illegally online, we are not able to track every single one of them.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We would track in terms of survey numbers; we look at how things develop.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I would highlight this: our objective is to see how best we can look after the well-being of our people.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I know that from a specific individual perspective, we may like to take a stronger position and say that we ban it and send a very clear signal that way.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The issue now is how to deal with a very real and practical problem, which is that people are gambling online.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Even with the ban being put in place, with MHA taking very active steps to ban new sites coming online, it is the nature of the Internet that we are not able to completely seal off that space.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We know that there are people gambling because there have been people and associated individuals arrested as a result of gambling illegally.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For those who are actually gambling online, when there are no safeguards, no safety valves, no safety measures put in place, they are being exposed to very real dangers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: One of the biggest concerns we have is criminal elements.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: What we do see, and we have arrested, is that it is not just the virtual gambling space, it extends to a very real world problem.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: There are punters, bookies, 	Page: 12 runners, agents collecting bet monies and extending credit lines.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: A lot of them, unfortunately, are involved with syndicated crime.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is not trivial from that perspective as well.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The Minister just mentioned that there are lots of ills of gambling,we cannot track and cannot seal it totally online.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The second question is: comparing total ban and now we have two operators who are licensed, what are the benefits that you are trying to achieve?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The global market for online gambling continues to grow.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Internet penetration, as I have mentioned, is pervasive in Singapore and that will continue to grow as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We all know that no ban on the Internet will completely seal things off.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Those that we are able to monitor, we will be able to take some action.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But it is a very large space and it is impossible to be able to completely ban that space.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: What happens to Singaporeans who are out there, who still feel that they want to be online and gambling and getting their fix in some shape and form?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is not just the social ills that come with that.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is also a very real concern with law and order issues because, as I have mentioned, criminal elements are involved.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: When you are betting online, whether on 4D, Toto, horse-racing and so on, there are bookies who collect the monies.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: There are agents who are there to promote.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: There are agents who are there to extend unlicensed moneylending facilities.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The real issues that we are concerned with do not really go away.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Our position is recognising a reality, which is that there are Singaporeans in that space.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are concerned that the numbers may grow as the space continues to proliferate and as the Internet continues to grow in terms of accessibility.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, for those who are there, we can at least provide some form of a safer space to manage that.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Members would remember, in the earlier years in the 1960s, we had a lot of illegal gambling, triad links and so on.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Then, we put in place Singapore Pools, the Tote Board, Turf Club, not-for-profit organisations.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: All the existing illegal online operators are there for profit and to exploit as much as they can.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But the whole issue here is to really recognise that some of these vices will not go away.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: How do I deal with a real world problem?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: How do we look out for the best interest of our people?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will want to continue, through public education and raising awareness, to dissuade Singaporeans from gambling in the first place and particularly online gambling.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But for those who are in that space, 	Page: 13 can we provide some form of outlet where there are safeguards put in place?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is what is happening in Hong Kong and Norway as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They have also studied very closely the effects of what they have done.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: What they have found from their assessment is that it has not proliferated and encouraged online gambling in a very big way, but it allows them some space to manage that.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: And that is the way we want to approach it.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, we share very similar concerns as Members do, which is to deal with the excesses of online gambling.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I just want to remind Members that Question No 2 will address some of the issues that you are also raising, so you can also reserve your supplementary questions for Question No 2.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I have a few supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The second question: at the Second Reading of the Bill, the then Minister for Social and Family Development also spoke of the prospect of online counselling.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Thirdly, beyond the requirements that are outlined in the Act, has the Government imposed any additional or specific directions on the Turf Club or Singapore Pools, in relation to the conduct, supervision and control of remote gambling in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In terms of the measures that are being put in place to deal with online gambling, the whole list of these has been highlighted.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, we have mentioned that, in terms of age limit, you have to be at least 21 years old to open a remote gambling account; persons with relevant casino exclusion will be prohibited from opening an account; the exempt operators will conduct periodic checks with NCPG and account holders who are found to be on any of the relevant casino exclusions will have their accounts closed; relevant casino exclusions include the Family Exclusion Order, the Third Party Exclusion Order and also Automatic Exclusion by law.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Page: 14 What are the daily funding and expenditure limits?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As an additional safeguard, as I have mentioned, any increase in limits takes effect from the next day, while decisions to decrease the limits will take effect immediately.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In terms of the Remote Responsible Gambling Programme, the exempt operators are required to implement remote responsible gambling programmes which would promote responsible gambling and informed play amongst players.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Just to illustrate: today, when someone goes to the outlet to buy 4D or Toto, he usually does not track, depending on whether he keeps his own excel spreadsheet or whatever he does to track his expenditure.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: He actually may have no clue how much he has been spending accumulatively over time.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: When they are online, that is something that would be made available and made obvious to the individuals concerned.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That could have a salutary effect, possibly for some of them.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For the operators themselves, there will be training of the staff.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The training programme will be put in place to train them to recognise the signs and harms of problem gambling.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Staff would be trained to promote responsible gambling and develop protocols for existing players who request for assistance, or to detect signs of problem gambling.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Additionally, there is a prevention of gambling inducement via advertising and promotions, so the exempt operators have to submit all materials, as mentioned earlier, for advertising and promotions to MSF for approval.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Essentially, no inducement of gambling, no depiction of gambling as a positive avenue, no misleading or false statements about chances of winnings, no appeal to vulnerable groups, including youths.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These are measures that we are looking at putting in place.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will constantly review them in terms of their effectiveness and whether things need to be tightened, or if there are new measures to be introduced.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In terms of the provision of counselling of various sorts, we will continue to look at whatever measures that may be possible.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The existing measures will continue to be there, but we will also explore different ways of providing support for the individuals who may need counselling and that would include online counselling.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But that is something that we are still looking at in terms of how that may take place.
